workflow_sequence.description: Administrator navigates to Tactic Type & Delivery Method admin section; frontend requests the full (unfiltered by active status) list of tactic types with nested delivery methods from the admin API

handshake_points.data_shape: GET /api/v1/admin/tactic-types -> AdminTacticTypeDto[] (Id, Name, IsActive, DisplayOrder, DeliveryMethods[])

workflow_sequence.description: Administrator toggles active/inactive on a tactic type or delivery method in the working draft; change is held in local UI state only (not yet persisted)

Administrator adds a new tactic type or a new delivery method (with Name, and for delivery methods: RequiresDigitalProvider / RequiresPrinter) to the working draft; frontend performs client-side duplicate check for immediate feedback
Administrator clicks Save; frontend submits the full set of draft changes (status toggles + new entities) to the backend, which validates business rules and persists them atomically

handshake_points.data_shape: PATCH /api/v1/admin/tactic-types -> SaveTacticTypeAdminChangesCommand { StatusToggles: [{EntityType, Id, IsActive}], NewTacticTypes: [{Name}], NewDeliveryMethods: [{Name, TacticTypeId, RequiresDigitalProvider, RequiresPrinter}] } -> SaveTacticTypeAdminChangesResponse
EF Core writes to TacticTypes and DeliveryMethods tables within a single transaction; unique constraint enforced on (DeliveryMethod.Name, TacticTypeId)

workflow_sequence.description: Backend invalidates the reference-data memory cache entries for TacticTypes and DeliveryMethods so that subsequent reads (admin and order form) reflect the new state immediately

handshake_points.data_shape: Remove cache keys: TacticTypes, TacticTypes:Admin, DeliveryMethods:All, DeliveryMethods:{tacticTypeId} for each affected TacticTypeId

workflow_sequence.description: Requestor opens the order form; read APIs return only active tactic types that have at least one active delivery method, and only active delivery methods within them, reflecting the administrator's changes

handshake_points.data_shape: GET /api/v1/reference/tactic-types, GET /api/v1/reference/delivery-methods -> filtered to IsActive=true, tactic types with zero active delivery methods excluded

workflow_sequence.description: Requestor views historical order that references a now-inactive tactic type or delivery method; historical read path resolves the reference directly by Id without applying the active-status filter, so the inactive value remains visible

handshake_points.data_shape: Historical order queries join TacticType/DeliveryMethod by Id (no soft-delete/hard-delete ever occurs, so FK integrity is preserved regardless of IsActive)

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Render list view of tactic types with nested delivery methods, active/inactive indicators, and toggle controls
new_responsibilities.intent: Display is a frontend concern; the UI shows current admin-facing state

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Maintain draft mode local state (pending toggles and new entries) until explicit Save, with a Discard action
new_responsibilities.intent: Sequence/UX of review-before-commit lives in the frontend per AC 'explicit save in drafting mode'

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Client-side optimistic duplicate-name check and max-length validation for immediate feedback
new_responsibilities.intent: Fast feedback loop for UX; not authoritative (backend re-validates)

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Disable/hide delete controls, exposing only inactive-toggle for removal semantics
new_responsibilities.intent: Adapts UI to the 'cannot delete, only deactivate' business rule surfaced by backend contract

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Authorize admin tactic-type/delivery-method endpoints to Admin role only
new_responsibilities.intent: Security enforcement belongs on the backend (Authorize attribute), consistent with AdminEntitiesController pattern

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Enforce uniqueness of (DeliveryMethod.Name, TacticTypeId) at command-handling time before persistence
new_responsibilities.intent: Business rule / data integrity enforcement is a backend responsibility, defensible zone ahead of the data layer

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Reject attempts to delete; only expose update-status operations (no DELETE endpoint)
new_responsibilities.intent: Constraint enforcement; frontend cannot be trusted to withhold delete requests

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Apply active-status + 'has at least one active delivery method' filtering in read/reference query handlers for non-admin (order form) consumers
new_responsibilities.intent: Filter hierarchy and scope of supported functionality is backend logic; admin queries bypass this filter

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Invalidate IMemoryCache entries for TacticTypes/DeliveryMethods on every admin write
new_responsibilities.intent: Cache ownership already resides in the backend per ADR 20251218-20; admin writes must not leave the 1-hour stale window uncontrolled

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist all requested toggles and creations from a single Save action atomically (single DB transaction)
new_responsibilities.intent: Handles the 'rapid status changes' and partial-failure edge cases; last-write-wins is acceptable per existing concurrency posture in this codebase

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Add IsActive (bit, default 1) to TacticTypes and DeliveryMethods tables
new_responsibilities.intent: Storage of the new domain concept lives in schema/model

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Add RequiresDigitalProvider and RequiresPrinter (bit, default 0) to DeliveryMethods table
new_responsibilities.intent: Storage of delivery method type attributes from the story's inputs

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Add a unique index on (DeliveryMethods.Name, DeliveryMethods.TacticTypeId)
new_responsibilities.intent: Data integrity constraint enforced at the database level as the last line of defense behind backend validation

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Never hard-delete TacticType/DeliveryMethod rows; FK relationships from Tactics remain RESTRICT
new_responsibilities.intent: Preserves historical order references per AC 'inactive tactic types remain visible in historical orders'

contracts.name: TacticTypeDeliveryMethodDataModel
contracts.description: Extends existing TacticType and DeliveryMethod domain models/tables with active-status and delivery-method-type attributes

changes.added: TacticType.IsActive (bool, default true); DeliveryMethod.IsActive (bool, default true); DeliveryMethod.RequiresDigitalProvider (bool, default false); DeliveryMethod.RequiresPrinter (bool, default false); unique index IX_DeliveryMethods_Name_TacticTypeId on DeliveryMethod(Name, TacticTypeId)
changes.modified: None (existing Id, Name, TacticTypeId, DisplayOrder columns unchanged)
changes.removed: None; no delete capability is added to the schema

contracts.name: GetAdminTacticTypesAPI
contracts.description: New admin-only read endpoint returning all tactic types (active and inactive) with nested delivery methods, for the admin list view

changes.added: GET /api/v1/admin/tactic-types -> AdminTacticTypeDto[] { Id, Name, IsActive, DisplayOrder, DeliveryMethods: [{ Id, Name, IsActive, RequiresDigitalProvider, RequiresPrinter, DisplayOrder }] }, [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")], follows AdminEntitiesController pattern

contracts.name: SaveTacticTypeAdminChangesAPI
contracts.description: New admin-only write endpoint that atomically applies all pending draft changes (status toggles + new tactic types + new delivery methods) from a single Save action

changes.added: PATCH /api/v1/admin/tactic-types -> SaveTacticTypeAdminChangesCommand { StatusToggles: [{ EntityType: 'TacticType'|'DeliveryMethod', Id, IsActive }], NewTacticTypes: [{ Name }], NewDeliveryMethods: [{ Name, TacticTypeId, RequiresDigitalProvider, RequiresPrinter }] } -> SaveTacticTypeAdminChangesResponse { UpdatedTacticTypes: AdminTacticTypeDto[] }; returns 409 with reasonCode on duplicate delivery method or validation error; [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]
changes.removed: None (no DELETE endpoint exists or is added, per 'cannot be deleted' constraint)

contracts.name: ReferenceTacticTypeAndDeliveryMethodReadAPIs
contracts.description: Existing GET /api/v1/reference/tactic-types and GET /api/v1/reference/delivery-methods endpoints, modified to filter out inactive records for requestor-facing consumption

changes.added: Filter clause: IsActive = true; TacticTypes additionally excluded when they have zero delivery methods with IsActive = true
changes.modified: GetTacticTypesQueryHandler and GetDeliveryMethodsQueryHandler now query only active rows and use distinct cache keys (e.g. 'TacticTypes:Active', 'DeliveryMethods:Active:{tacticTypeId}') so admin (unfiltered) and requestor (filtered) results are never cross-contaminated in cache

contracts.name: DraftModeSaveInteraction
contracts.description: Frontend accumulates changes client-side and submits them in a single batch on explicit Save, rather than auto-saving each toggle/add individually

changes.added: Client-side draft state (pending toggles, pending new entities) held until Save; Discard action resets to last-fetched server state
changes.modified: None (no prior interaction pattern existed since the UI is a placeholder)

architectural_decisions.decision: Follow the existing AdminEntitiesController pattern (CQRS via MediatR, [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")], record-based Commands/Queries) for the new admin tactic-type endpoints rather than introducing a new admin framework
architectural_decisions.justification: Minimizes new architectural surface area and keeps admin endpoints consistent and discoverable
architectural_decisions.basis: Pattern precedent in src/api/src/TacticManagement.Api/Controllers/AdminEntitiesController.cs (Story 25A OpCo Entity Admin)
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: N/A - architectural precedent choice, not a story question

architectural_decisions.decision: Implement Save as a single batch endpoint (PATCH with StatusToggles + NewTacticTypes + NewDeliveryMethods) instead of one call per toggle/add
architectural_decisions.justification: Matches the story's explicit drafting-mode requirement (AC: 'changes are saved explicitly with a save action') and gives the backend a single transaction boundary to guarantee atomicity of related toggles
architectural_decisions.basis: Explicit Architectural Change from Story (draft mode requirement)
architectural_decisions.impact: New composite command/handler and DTOs; frontend maintains local draft state instead of calling PATCH per field
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should changes be auto-saved or require explicit save action? -> Explicit save; see questions_addressed

architectural_decisions.decision: Reuse ADR 20251218-20 sliding-expiration IMemoryCache strategy, and explicitly invalidate affected keys on every admin write rather than waiting for expiration
architectural_decisions.justification: The ADR's 1-hour sliding TTL is fine for rare reference-data changes done outside this story, but this story is precisely the trigger for those changes; admins expect toggles to take effect immediately in the order form (AC: active/inactive visibility)
architectural_decisions.basis: ADR 20251218-20-reference-data-memory-caching.md (Future Considerations: 'Cache Invalidation Endpoint... allow admins to force cache refresh')
architectural_decisions.impact: SaveTacticTypeAdminChanges handler takes a dependency on IMemoryCache to Remove() the relevant keys after successful persistence

architectural_decisions.decision: Use separate cache key namespaces/entries for admin (unfiltered) vs requestor (active-only) reference reads
architectural_decisions.justification: Prevents an admin's unfiltered admin-list fetch from being served from or polluting the requestor-facing active-only cache entry, and vice versa
architectural_decisions.basis: Pattern precedent in ADR 20251218-20 which already differentiates 'Entities:{Type}:All' (admin) from OpCo-filtered keys
architectural_decisions.impact: New cache key constants in GetTacticTypesQueryHandler/GetDeliveryMethodsQueryHandler; new admin query handler uses its own key

architectural_decisions.decision: No DELETE endpoint or hard-delete capability is implemented for TacticType/DeliveryMethod; only IsActive can be set false
architectural_decisions.justification: Directly required by AC ('cannot be deleted, only marked inactive') and protects FK integrity for historical Tactics referencing these rows
architectural_decisions.basis: Explicit Architectural Change from Story (constraint AC)
architectural_decisions.impact: Controller exposes no delete route; repository has no delete method for these entities
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How should the system handle deletion requests if deletion is not allowed? -> No delete route exists at all; see questions_addressed

architectural_decisions.decision: Concurrent admin edits use last-write-wins with no optimistic concurrency token in this iteration
architectural_decisions.justification: Consistent with the codebase's existing concurrency posture (no RowVersion/ETag pattern observed on other admin-managed reference entities such as Entity/OpCo); introducing optimistic concurrency here would be a scope increase beyond what the story asks for
architectural_decisions.basis: Pattern precedent: UpdateEntityCommandHandler/Entity model have no concurrency token
architectural_decisions.impact: No RowVersion column added; edge case 'concurrent edits' resolves as last save wins, consistent with existing admin entity behavior
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Given two administrators are editing tactic types simultaneously When both attempt to save changes Then the last save wins or conflict is detected -> Last save wins; see questions_addressed

questions_addressed.question: What is the maximum length for tactic type names and delivery method names?
questions_addressed.answer: 100 characters for both TacticType.Name and DeliveryMethod.Name
questions_addressed.justification: Consistent, sufficient length for descriptive names while bounding storage and UI layout
questions_addressed.basis: Existing HasMaxLength(100) convention already applied to TacticType.Name and DeliveryMethod.Name in TacticDbContext.cs

questions_addressed.question: Should changes be auto-saved or require explicit save action?
questions_addressed.answer: Explicit save action; the UI operates in draft mode and only persists on Save, with a Discard option to revert
questions_addressed.justification: Explicitly required by acceptance criterion 'Changes are saved explicitly with a save action in drafting mode'

questions_addressed.question: What happens when an administrator tries to mark all delivery methods of a tactic type as inactive?
questions_addressed.answer: It is allowed; the system does not block this action. The resulting side effect is that the parent tactic type will no longer appear on the requestor order form (per the 'no delivery methods shown' rule), but it remains visible and editable in the admin list. No warning is required in this iteration.
questions_addressed.justification: The story's edge case only covers a tactic type with a single delivery method remaining visible in the admin list when inactivated; there is no stated requirement to block or warn on this admin action, and blocking would add scope not requested
questions_addressed.basis: administer-tactic-types.analysis.json edge_cases[0] and acceptance_criteria[7] ('Tactic types with no delivery methods are not shown on the front end') define the visible behavior without requiring a blocking rule

questions_addressed.question: Should there be an audit trail for tactic type and delivery method changes?
questions_addressed.answer: No dedicated audit table in this iteration; sufficient traceability is provided via structured logging (Information level) of every toggle/create with adminUserId and correlationId, following the existing pattern used for admin Entity changes and the Field Authorization Service's audit logging approach.
questions_addressed.justification: No compliance requirement for a persisted audit trail was stated in the story; existing admin write paths (Entity, OpCo) rely on logs, not a dedicated table, so this stays consistent with current practice
questions_addressed.basis: Pattern precedent: AdminEntitiesController/UpdateEntityCommandHandler rely on ILogger; ADR 20260127-28 documents logging-based audit trail as sufficient for authorization decisions

questions_addressed.question: How should the system handle deletion requests if deletion is not allowed?
questions_addressed.answer: No DELETE endpoint is exposed for TacticType or DeliveryMethod at all; the API surface only offers status-toggle via the Save endpoint. The frontend never renders a delete control, only an active/inactive toggle.
questions_addressed.justification: Prevents the question from arising at the API layer entirely, which is simpler and more secure than accepting a delete request and returning an error
questions_addressed.basis: administer-tactic-types.analysis.json acceptance_criteria[9] ('cannot be deleted, only marked inactive')

questions_addressed.question: Given two administrators are editing tactic types simultaneously When both attempt to save changes Then the last save wins or conflict is detected
questions_addressed.answer: Last save wins; no optimistic concurrency (RowVersion/ETag) is introduced in this iteration
questions_addressed.justification: Matches existing behavior of comparable admin-managed reference entities (Entity, OpCo) which also have no concurrency token; adding one here would be inconsistent scope creep for a low-frequency admin workflow
questions_addressed.basis: Pattern precedent: UpdateEntityCommandHandler and Entity/OpCo domain models have no concurrency token
